item.title: Rare concert recordings are landing on the Internet Archive
item.description:
📝 So far, about 2,500 of these tapes have been posted on the Internet Archive, including some rare gems like a Nirvana performance from 1989. For many of these recordings, Jacobs was using pretty mediocre equipment, but the volunteer audio engineers working with the Internet Archive have made these tapes sound great. Sometimes, the internet is good.
🔗 Read more: https://techcrunch.com/2026/04/13/thousands-of-rare-concert-recordings-are-landing-on-the-internet-archive-listen-now/

item.title: For the First Time in the U.S., Renewables Generate More Power Than Natural Gas
item.description:
📝 , Renewables Generate More Power Than Natural Gas Pexels In a first last month, renewables supplied more power to the U. However, rising power demand is complicating the transition away from fossil fuels by extending the lives of many aging coal power plants. Only four coal power plants retired generators last year, according to the EIA.
🔗 Read more: https://e360.yale.edu/digest/us-renewables-natural-gas-coal

item.title: Google, Microsoft, Meta All Tracking You Even When You Opt Out
item.description:
📝 The webXray California Privacy Audit viewed web traffic on more than 7,000 popular websites in California in the month of March and found that most tech companies ignore when a user asks to opt-out of cookie tracking. ’ This means Google should not return cookies,” the audit said. webXray is an independent technology company that runs a search engine that lets people look for privacy violations on the internet.
🔗 Read more: https://www.404media.co/google-microsoft-meta-all-tracking-you-even-when-you-opt-out-according-to-an-independent-audit/
